title: The intention
hookLine: every prayer begins in the heart, not on the tongue

lines: TWO PEOPLE, ONE TWENTY, ONE BOX.
cards: Two people drop a twenty in the same charity box. One does it because someone important is watching. The other, because of a child she saw in the news this morning.

From the outside, nothing tells them apart: same twenty, same box. For the next stretch, this path turns from stories to practices, the things Muslims actually do, starting with the prayer, salat, step by step.
And the first step of the prayer isn't a movement or a word. It happens where no one can see it.

teach.h: NIYYAH: WHAT YOU MEAN BY IT.
teach.b: The word is niyyah: intention, what you mean by what you're about to do. Sahih al-Bukhari opens with a hadith about it.

The Prophet ﷺ said, in its meaning: actions are only by their intentions, and each person gets only what they intended. Then he gives an example. Two people make the same journey, the hijra you just followed to Medina.
One goes for Allah and His messenger. The other goes for something of this world, or to marry someone. Same road, same dust, different journeys.
So before every prayer, a Muslim forms the intention: this is the noon prayer, four units, for Allah. Where does that happen?

teach.h: IN THE HEART, NOT ON THE TONGUE.
teach.b: The scholars place it in the heart. You don't have to say it out loud; if your heart knows what it's doing, the niyyah is there.
Some, especially in the Shafi'i school, recommend saying it quietly as well, to help the heart focus. Either way, it isn't a formula. It's a turning.
A hadith in Sahih Muslim says Allah does not look at your bodies or your faces, but at your hearts and your deeds.
And one in Bukhari is tender: if someone intends a good deed and then can't do it, it is still written for them as a good deed.
The intention itself counts. In that reading, an ordinary day can become worship when it's meant.
The Qur'an gives words for that: “Lo! my worship and my sacrifice and my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the Worlds.” Living, too, not just praying.

how: Before each prayer, fast or act of worship, Muslims form an intention in the heart, naming to themselves which prayer or deed it is and that it is for Allah; scholars differ on whether also saying it quietly is recommended.

games.q: two people make the same journey to Medina. one goes for Allah and His messenger, the other to marry someone there. according to the hadith, what did each one get?
games.why: actions are by intentions, and each person gets what they intended: same road, different journeys (Bukhari 1).

practice: Before the sit begins, ask yourself one quiet question: why am I doing this? Not the right answer, the real one: to feel calmer, to learn, to be close to Allah, because someone I love prays.
Let the answer be honest, then begin on purpose; if you pray, you can make your intention for Allah.
